summary: Canadian-born magnetic healer D. D. Palmer invented chiropractic in Iowa in 1895, claiming a dead doctor's ghost revealed it and later recasting it as a religion to dodge licensing; the story follows its modern harms, from neck strokes to infant adjustments.

evidence.note: Palmer born in a vanished town near Toronto, Canada; childhood segment follows
brothers leave Canada for the US in 1865
September encounter with deaf janitor Harvey Lillard, the claimed first adjustment
Palmer school founded 1897 in Davenport, Iowa
Palmer credits a dead doctor's ghost contacted in a seance with the method
B. J. Palmer takes over the school and pushes salesmanship and rented devices
Palmer and son oppose vaccination as medicine professionalises
1911 letter modelling chiropractic as a religion after Christian Science
Palmer dies October 1913; his book The Chiropractor appears in 1914
20th-century licensing fights and the Doctor of Chiropractic degree
stroke in a six-year-old and a video of an infant spinal adjustment
modern deaths and strokes linked to neck manipulation, into the 2010s

notes: Transcript gives the first adjustment only as a September day; 1895 is from general knowledge, as is Palmer's 1845 birth year (transcript audio garbles the date). child-abuse theme reflects the segment on chiropractic treatment of a child and an infant, not deliberate abuse; reviewer may prefer to drop it. covered_span ends 2019 for the modern-practice segment.
